title: NSS 79th Round - Household Listing & Selection Procedures
description: Comprehensive competency test on First Stage Unit (FSU) delineation, hamlet-group formation, circular systematic sampling, and Schedule 0.0 listing protocols.

questions.question: In rural areas for the current NSS Round, what constitutes the First Stage Unit (FSU)?
options: A Census Village as per the 2011 Population Census
An Urban Frame Survey (UFS) block with 100-120 households
A cluster of exactly 8 households selected via SRSWOR
The entire Gram Panchayat administrative boundary
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: In rural sectors, the 2011 Census village is taken as the First Stage Unit (FSU). Option B describes the urban FSU (UFS block). Option C describes the Ultimate Stage Unit (USU) sample size. Option D is incorrect because Gram Panchayats typically encompass multiple villages.
questions.referencePassage: In the rural sector, the First Stage Units (FSUs) are the 2011 Census villages, whereas in the urban sector, the FSUs are the latest Urban Frame Survey (UFS) blocks.

questions.question: Suppose an investigator encounters a large rural village with an estimated present population of 2,100 during the listing stage. According to NSS guidelines, how many hamlet-groups (hg) must be formed?
options: 1 hamlet-group (No subdivision required)
2 hamlet-groups
3 hamlet-groups
4 hamlet-groups
questions.explanation: Option C is correct: According to NSS listing rules: population < 1,200 requires 1 hg; 1,200 to 1,799 requires 2 hg; 1,800 to 2,399 requires 3 hg; and 2,400 to 2,999 requires 4 hg. Since 2,100 falls in the range 1,800-2,399, exactly 3 hamlet-groups must be formed.
questions.referencePassage: If the estimated present population of the village is 1,800 to 2,399, the number of hamlet-groups to be formed is 3; if 2,400 to 2,999, the number of hamlet-groups to be formed is 4.

questions.question: Which sampling technique is officially prescribed for selecting the 8 Ultimate Stage Units (Households) from the listing frame in Schedule 0.0?
options: Circular Systematic Sampling with a random start
Simple Random Sampling with Replacement (SRSWR)
Purposive Quota Sampling based on investigator discretion
Single-stage Cluster Sampling of the nearest contiguous dwellings
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Official NSS methodology mandates Circular Systematic Sampling with a random start across the stratified household listing frame to ensure unbiased probability selection.
questions.referencePassage: In each selected FSU/hg, exactly 8 sample households shall be selected by Circular Systematic Sampling with a random start for canvassing Schedule 10.3.

questions.question: In NSS estimation under Probability Proportional to Size with Replacement (PPSWR), what represents the sampling multiplier for the i-th FSU?
options: M_i = Z / (n * Z_i), where Z is stratum total size and Z_i is FSU size
M_i = (n * Z_i) / Z, the direct probability of inclusion
M_i = N / n, the simple unweighted expansion factor
M_i = (N * n) / (Z_i * H), adjusted for total households
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: The inclusion probability for an FSU under PPSWR is p_i = Z_i / Z. For a sample of n FSUs, the design weight/multiplier is 1 / (n * p_i) = Z / (n * Z_i).
questions.referencePassage: For PPSWR sampling of FSUs, the sampling weight (multiplier) in the estimation formula is given by M_i = Z / (n_s * Z_si).

questions.question: If an investigator discovers during field scrutiny that a selected sample household has migrated permanently, what is the mandatory protocol?
options: Record casualty status and select a substitute household strictly from the standby random selection list
Canvass the immediate adjacent neighbor household informally
Omit the sample record and re-weight remaining sample households post-facto
Leave the schedule blank and mark the hamlet as non-existent
questions.competencyName: Field Survey Team Management & High-Performance Supervision
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Official survey protocol prohibits informal ad-hoc substitution. If a casualty occurs, it must be officially coded, and substitution must be performed using the predefined alternate random selection sequence.
questions.referencePassage: In case a selected sample household cannot be canvassed due to permanent migration or refusal, substitution shall be made strictly in order of selection from the standby sample frame.

title: Consumer Price Index (CPI Base 2012) - Methodology & Aggregation
description: Assessment of price collection, Modified Laspeyres index formulation, item baskets, weighting diagrams, and quality adjustment standards.

questions.question: Which index formula is officially utilized by MoSPI to aggregate elementary price relatives into subgroup and group Consumer Price Indices?
options: Modified Laspeyres price index formula with base-period expenditure weights
Paasche price index formula utilizing current-period consumption quantities
Fisher's Ideal Geometric Mean index formula
Carli unweighted arithmetic mean of price relatives
questions.competencyName: Index Numbers & Price Statistics (CPI, IIP, WPI)
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: MoSPI's CPI (Rural, Urban, Combined) uses the Modified Laspeyres formula, aggregating elementary price relatives with fixed base-period consumption expenditure weights from the Consumer Expenditure Survey (CES 2011-12).
questions.referencePassage: The all-India and state-level CPI indices are compiled using the Modified Laspeyres Index formula using the weighting diagram derived from the Consumer Expenditure Survey 2011-12.

questions.question: In the All-India CPI (Combined) basket, which commodity group holds the largest percentage weight?
options: Food and Beverages (approx. 45.86%)
Housing (approx. 21.60%)
Fuel and Light (approx. 15.20%)
Miscellaneous Services (approx. 32.10%)
questions.competencyName: Index Numbers & Price Statistics (CPI, IIP, WPI)
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Food and Beverages constitutes the largest group weight in the all-India CPI basket at approximately 45.86% (over 54% in rural and 36% in urban).
questions.referencePassage: Food and Beverages group carries the highest weight of 45.86% in the All-India Combined CPI basket.

questions.question: When a specific brand or item specification is permanently discontinued in a selected market center, what is the prescribed procedure for the statistical investigator?
options: Identify the most comparable substitute item with highest current sales volume and record overlapping prices for base-period linking
Drop the item entirely and rescale the weights of the remaining items
Carry forward the last recorded price indefinitely
Insert the average price of all items across the entire district
questions.competencyName: Index Numbers & Price Statistics (CPI, IIP, WPI)
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Official price statistics guidelines mandate selecting the most popular comparable substitute and collecting simultaneous prices for overlap linking to prevent artificial price jumps.
questions.referencePassage: In case of permanent non-availability of a selected item specification, a closely comparable substitute specification shall be selected with overlap pricing.

questions.question: Under the X-13ARIMA-SEATS seasonal adjustment protocol used for economic indicators, what is the primary objective of the regARIMA pre-adjustment step?
options: To estimate and remove deterministic calendar effects (trading day variation, moving holidays, leap years) and detect outlier anomalies
To smooth out all long-term economic trend growth
To convert nominal index values into real chained volume measures
To impute missing data using linear interpolation
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: The regARIMA module models calendar effects (trading day and national holidays like Diwali) and identifies additive/transitory outliers prior to X-11 filter decomposition.
questions.referencePassage: The regARIMA pre-treatment models deterministic calendar effects, moving holidays, and outlier interventions prior to seasonal filter application.

title: National Data Governance & Statistical Disclosure Control (NDGFP)
description: Evaluation of microdata anonymization standards, k-anonymity thresholds, DDI metadata registries, and UN-FPOS ethical principles.

questions.question: Under the National Data Governance Framework Policy (NDGFP), what minimum k-anonymity threshold is mandated prior to releasing public survey microdata?
options: k >= 5 (Each combination of quasi-identifiers must be shared by at least 5 distinct individuals)
k >= 2 (Basic pairwise obscurity)
k >= 20 (Mandatory only for enterprise data)
No k-anonymity required if direct names are removed
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Under NDGFP standards, anonymized public microdata files must satisfy k-anonymity with k >= 5 to prevent re-identification attacks via linked auxiliary databases.
questions.referencePassage: Departments must apply k-anonymity (k >= 5) and l-diversity algorithms to prevent re-identification of survey respondents or enterprise establishments.

questions.question: Under the Statistical Data and Metadata eXchange (SDMX) framework, what constitutes a Data Structure Definition (DSD)?
options: A formal specification defining the Dimensions, Attributes, and Primary Measure of a statistical dataflow
A relational database schema script for PostgreSQL tables
The private encryption key used to sign official PDF releases
The user access control list for departmental server logins
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: In SDMX, a Data Structure Definition (DSD) defines the structure of multidimensional statistical datasets including Dimensions (identifiers), Attributes (metadata), and Measures (values).
questions.referencePassage: The SDMX Data Structure Definition (DSD) specifies the concept scheme, code lists, dimensions, and attributes required to interpret statistical time series data.

questions.question: Under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008, what is the legal mandate regarding individual respondent information disclosed in official schedules?
options: It is strictly confidential and inadmissible as evidence in court or for taxation/prosecution against the respondent
It can be shared with law enforcement agencies upon written police request
It becomes public property and can be published in unit-level identified form after 1 year
It may be used by the Income Tax department for audit reconciliations
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: Section 9 and 10 of the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 explicitly protect statistical confidentiality; individual returns cannot be used for taxation, law enforcement, or court prosecution.
questions.referencePassage: Information collected under the Collection of Statistics Act 2008 shall be used solely for statistical purposes and is strictly inadmissible as evidence in any legal proceeding against the respondent.

questions.question: Which international framework provides the 8 core phases for modeling official statistical business workflows (Specify Needs, Design, Build, Collect, Process, Analyze, Disseminate, Evaluate)?
options: Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM)
ISO 9001 Quality Management System
COBIT IT Governance Framework
UN-SEEA Ecosystem Accounting Framework
questions.competencyName: Statistical Audit, Process Validation & System Documentation
questions.explanation: Option A is correct: The UNECE Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM v5.1) defines the 8 standard phases of official statistical production adopted across MoSPI.
questions.referencePassage: The Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM) standardizes the 8 end-to-end phases of official statistical production from user needs identification to dissemination and evaluation.
